value: "The flagship dataset of the Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable (also rendered \"Exploratory\") Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI) project, published on the FAIRhub data portal. It consists of multimodal data collected from individuals with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), harmonized across three data collection sites (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, and University of Washington). The dataset is designed for downstream artificial intelligence and machine learning research into salutogenesis, the pathway from disease back to health, in T2DM. Recruitment sampling aimed at an approximately equal distribution of participants across diabetes severity, and the acquisition protocol spans multiple domains (survey data, physical measurements, clinical data, imaging data, wearable device data, environmental sensing) to enable analyses not feasible with claims or electronic health record data. This record describes version 3.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3), made available on FAIRhub on 2025-11-17, containing data from 2280 participants collected between 2023-07-19 and 2025-05-01, comprising 356,343 files totalling approximately 3.82 TB. The dataset also has an alternative title, \"AI-READI dataset\". Two earlier versions exist (1.0.0 and 2.0.0); FAIRhub marks version 2.0.0 as no longer accessible. Each release is distributed as a publicly accessible set stripped of protected health information and, per project documentation, a controlled-access set containing more sensitive elements."

value: "A multimodal dataset collected by the Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable (also rendered \"Exploratory\") Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI) project, one of four data generation projects of the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program. The dataset consists of data collected from individuals with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), harmonized across three data collection sites (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, University of Washington). Version 3.0.0 contains data from 2280 participants collected between July 19, 2023 and May 1, 2025, comprising 356,343 files and approximately 3.82 TB. Modalities include survey/clinical data collected through REDCap and mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model, 12-lead electrocardiography, retinal photography, OCT, OCTA and fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy in DICOM, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable physical activity monitoring, and custom home environmental sensor data. The composition was designed for downstream AI/ML research on salutogenesis (the pathway from disease to health) in T2DM, with recruitment sampling aimed at approximately equal distribution across diabetes severity and, as an overall enrollment goal, across race/ethnicity and sex. The public release contains no protected health information; sex, race/ethnicity and medication information are removed from the public set and held under controlled access."

The dataset contains data from 2280 participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), collected between 19 July 2023 and 1 May 2025 at three US sites (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, and University of Washington) and harmonized across sites. Modalities include REDCap survey and clinical data mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model, 12-lead electrocardiography, retinal photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy (FLIO), continuous glucose monitoring, wearable activity monitoring, and custom indoor environmental sensing. The release comprises 356,343 files totalling approximately 3.82 TB, organized following the Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1. The dataset contains no protected health information; information on participant sex, race/ethnicity and medications used has been removed from this release. The stated goal is to enable AI/ML research into salutogenesis (the pathway from disease back to health) in T2DM."
